cohort: Nulliparous women aged at least 18 years, with a singleton gestation and a Bishop score of 5 or less, enrolled between 38 0/7 and 38 6/7 weeks of gestation.
finding: Elective induction of labor in nulliparous women with a Bishop score of 5 or less resulted in a higher cesarean delivery rate (30.5%) compared with expectant management (17.7%), but this did not achieve a twofold increase.
mod_finding: Elective induction of labor did not double the rate of cesarean delivery compared with expectant management.
gest_age: Participants were enrolled between 38 0/7 and 38 6/7 weeks of gestation, with inductions not performed before 39 0/7 weeks of gestation.
